originalTitle: House committee launches investigation into Republican lawmaker amid domestic abuse allegations – as it happened
summary: Max Miller says he has ‘nothing to hide’ amid domestic abuse allegations made against him by his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, daughter of Republican Ohio senator Bernie Moreno
content: Thanks for following our live coverage of the second Trump administration. Stay tuned to our blog dedicated to the US midterm primary elections, where we’ll be watching the latest developments in Michigan, Kansas, Missouri, Virginia and Washington. Here are the highlights for today: The US Senate judiciary committee voted along party lines to advance Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general after he confirmed in writing that a planned $1.8bn slush fund for Donald Trump’s allies was dead. Experts say, however, that Trump could easily reverse the deal. More here. Max Miller, a US Republican representative from Ohio, is facing a rising groundswell of resignation calls from his own party over domestic abuse allegations after his ex-father-in-law, Bernie Moreno, a GOP senator, said he was unfit to serve in Congress. The House ethics committee announced it will launch an investigation into allegations that Miller “may have engaged in domestic violence and abuse or illegal drug use in violation of the code of official conduct or any other applicable standard of conduct” after the embattled Republican said he had “nothing to hide” and welcomed the investigation. More here. Jay Clayton has been sworn in as the US’s top spy after a contentious Senate confirmation hearing during which ⁠he refused to directly ⁠acknowledge that Donald Trump lost the 2020 presidential election. The oath of office was administered to Clayton on Tuesday by the treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, in the Oval Office as the president looked on and applauded. More here. An attorney for the former Olympic canoeist who was charged with vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool has said that “all options are on table” for legal recourse after prosecutors recently abandoned the case abruptly. David Hearn “has a number of potential remedies” after being prosecuted in connection with pool damage now attributed to faulty work by a contractor, attorney Steven Levin said in a statement. More here. A New York law banning US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents from wearing face coverings and requiring that they wear visible identification has been put on hold by a federal judge. But a state law prohibiting cooperation between local police departments and ICE has been allowed to stand. More here. Answering whether the release of a link containing private photographs of his daughter was reckless, Max Miller said that the incident “is being taken very much out of context.” “This is once again a very salacious headline,” Miller said. “I didn’t do this. My attorney took full responsibility. I believe that it’s awful. There was never any intent to do that.” Miller was also pressed by Jake Tapper on whether he believed the three women accusing him of violent behavior were all lying. “For no second am I going to sit here and continue to be debased by false and baseless allegations and be pushed out of a seat I have worked so hard to represent and done a terrific job for our community,” Miller said. “I’ve been a good legislator. All they’re trying to do is create rumor mills without evidence.” Asked whether he would consider dropping out of the race for the sake of his own mental health and his daughter’s well-being, Miller said he is “never going to give up.” “My daughter is going to grow up one day, and she’s going to see all of this, and she’s not going to see that her father caved to political and social media pressures,” Miller said. In an interview with CNN’s Jake Tapper, embattled Ohio representative Max Miller rejected claims from Senator Bernie Moreno (his former father-in-law) that Miller withheld his daughter’s favorite stuffed toy during a custody exchange. “I would agree that if that were true, that would be incredibly disturbing,” Miller told Tapper on Tuesday. “This is nothing more than an individual who’s being politically vindictive.” Moreno has called for Miller to withdraw from his re-election bid amid allegations of domestic abuse and seek professional help. On Tuesday, he described the experience as “truly the seventh level of hell” for his family. An instructor at the University of Maryland, Baltimore who only just received a “teacher of the year” award has been arrested by federal immigration agents under the command of the Trump administration. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials detained Berhanu Kibret, an instructor at the university’s pharmacy school, at the Dallas-Fort Worth airport in Texas, according to multiple news reports. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, confirmed Kibret’s arrest, citing an expired visa – but it stopped short of providing a location. In a statement, the University of Maryland said Kibret was arrested while returning from a meeting of the American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy, where he received a “teacher of the year” award. “Dr Kibret has a valid work authorization, so it is our hope that any issues surrounding his status will be quickly resolved and that he will be permitted to continue his work at the University of Maryland School of Pharmacy,” the institution added, according to CBS. The Associated Press is reporting that the Trump administration has revoked the visa of Brazil’s ambassador to the United States in retaliation for Brazil’s denial of visas last month for two American diplomats who sought to visit the country ahead of upcoming elections as well as Brazil’s stalling on approving President Donald Trump’s nominee to be ambassador in Brazil. The state department said the decision was a reciprocal response to Brazil’s move and officials said the step had been delayed several times to give Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva room to back down, something he did not do. Officials said it could be quickly reversed if Brazil takes appropriate action and accepts Trump’s ambassadorial choice. chineseContent: 感谢您关注我们对特朗普第二届政府的现场报道。请继续关注我们致力于美国中期初选的博客，我们将在其中关注密歇根州、堪萨斯州、密苏里州、弗吉尼亚州和华盛顿州的最新动态。今天的亮点如下：在托德·布兰奇以书面形式确认为唐纳德·特朗普盟友提供的 18 亿美元行贿基金计划已被取消后，美国参议院司法委员会按照党派路线投票推进了托德·布兰奇的司法部长提名。然而专家表示，特朗普可以轻易推翻该协议。更多这里。来自俄亥俄州的美国共和党众议员马克斯·米勒(Max Miller)在他的前岳父、共和党参议员伯尼·莫雷诺(Bernie Moreno)表示他不适合在国会任职后，面临着党内因家庭暴力指控而要求辞职的呼声高涨。众议院道德委员会宣布将对米勒“可能违反官方行为准则或任何其他适用行为标准，从事家庭暴力和虐待或非法吸毒”的指控展开调查，此前这位四面楚歌的共和党人表示他“没有什么可隐瞒的”并欢迎调查。更多这里。杰伊·克莱顿 (Jay Clayton) 在一场颇具争议的参议院确认听证会上宣誓就任美国最高间谍，在听证会上，他拒绝直接承认唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 输掉了 2020 年总统选举。周二，财政部长斯科特·贝森特在椭圆形办公室为克莱顿宣誓就职，总统在一旁观看并鼓掌。更多这里。这位被指控破坏林肯纪念堂倒影池的前奥运会皮划艇运动员的律师表示，在检察官最近突然放弃此案后，“所有选择都在考虑”，以寻求法律追索。大卫
